beats.text: Part a. The calibration energy is five point zero zero times one point two zero times three hundred: one thousand eight hundred joules. The calibration factor is one thousand eight hundred joules divided by three point zero zero degrees: six hundred joules per degree.

Now a plausibility check. The water alone would need one hundred and twenty-five point zero grams times four point one eight: five hundred and twenty-two point five joules per degree. The calibration factor is larger, which makes sense, because the cup, the thermometer and the stirrer absorb some energy too. A calibration factor smaller than the water alone would suggest an error. Three marks: the energy, the calibration factor, and the check.
